title: Blocking AI crawlers doesn't stop citations - new data shows why
summary: Blocking AI crawlers doesn't stop citations - new data shows why    PPC Land
editorial_override: Blocking AI crawlers doesnt stop citations — contrarian data on crawling vs AI training
post_en:
Blocking AI crawlers doesn't stop them from citing your content. New data proves it.

This challenges everything we thought we knew about robots.txt and AI training:

The findings:
→ Sites that block major AI crawlers still appear in AI-generated answers
→ Citation rates are nearly identical whether you block or allow crawling
→ AI models retain information from pre-block training data indefinitely
→ New AI systems access cached/archived versions of blocked content

What this means:

robots.txt was designed for a world where search engines respected "don't index this." AI doesn't work that way.

Three uncomfortable truths:
1. Once your data is in a training set, blocking the crawler is like closing the barn door after the horse left
2. AI companies are building on data collected BEFORE blocks were implemented
3. The legal frameworks assume blocking = protection. The data says otherwise.

For publishers and content owners: blocking crawlers gives the ILLUSION of control without actual protection.

For data infrastructure: this reshapes the entire compliance conversation. If blocking doesn't work, what does?

The answer is shifting toward:
• Licensing agreements with enforcement mechanisms
• Technical measures beyond robots.txt (rate limiting, auth walls)
• Legal frameworks that address training data, not just crawling

The robots.txt era of AI governance is over. What comes next will be more complex, more expensive, and more effective.

#AITrainingData #WebCrawling #DataGovernance
post_ru:

Это бросает вызов всему, что мы знали о robots.txt и обучении AI:

→ Сайты, блокирующие AI-краулеров, всё равно появляются в AI-ответах
→ Частота цитирования почти идентична — блокируете или нет
→ AI-модели хранят информацию из до-блокировочных данных бессрочно
→ Новые AI-системы берут кешированные/архивные версии заблокированного контента

Три неудобные правды:
1. Данные уже в тренировочном сете — блокировка краулера как закрыть дверь после ухода лошади
2. AI-компании строят на данных, собранных ДО блокировок
3. Правовые рамки предполагают: блокировка = защита. Данные говорят иначе.

Для издателей: блокировка даёт ИЛЛЮЗИЮ контроля без реальной защиты.

Ответ смещается к:
• Лицензионным соглашениям с механизмами enforcement
• Техническим мерам за пределами robots.txt
• Правовым рамкам, адресующим training data, а не просто краулинг

Эра robots.txt в AI-governance закончилась. Следующий этап будет сложнее, дороже и эффективнее.

#AITrainingData #WebCrawling #DataGovernance

title: Online bot traffic will exceed human traffic by 2027, Cloudflare CEO says
summary: Online bot traffic will exceed human traffic by 2027, Cloudflare CEO says    MSN
editorial_override: Cloudflare CEO: bot traffic > human traffic by 2027 — core bot traffic narrative
post_en:
Cloudflare's CEO confirmed it again: online bot traffic will exceed human traffic by 2027.

This isn't speculation anymore. It's an extrapolation from the traffic patterns Cloudflare sees across 20% of the internet.

The acceleration:
→ 2024: Bots were ~47% of all web traffic (Imperva data)
→ 2025: AI agents pushed bot traffic past 50% on many Cloudflare-protected sites
→ 2026: The crossover is happening on high-value commercial sites first
→ 2027: Global crossover — more machines browsing than humans

What's different about 2027 bots vs 2024 bots:

Old bots: Simple scripts making predictable requests
New bots: AI agents that browse like humans, make purchasing decisions, negotiate prices, and interact with content

The infrastructure implications are massive:
1. Website analytics become unreliable without bot filtering
2. A/B testing results are contaminated by machine visitors
3. Ad impressions served to bots are pure waste
4. Conversion funnels include non-human "customers"

For data infrastructure providers, this creates a paradox: the web is generating more data than ever, but a growing percentage of that data is machine-generated noise.

The companies that can separate signal from noise — real humans from sophisticated bots — will define the next era of web infrastructure.

#BotTraffic #Cloudflare #WebInfrastructure

title: Show HN: Gecit – DPI bypass using eBPF sock_ops, no proxy or VPN
summary: Article URL: https://github.com/boratanrikulu/gecit Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47650894 Points: 8 # Comments: 2
editorial_override: DPI bypass using eBPF — proxy/censorship bypass innovation, no VPN needed
post_en:
A new tool bypasses Deep Packet Inspection without a proxy or VPN. It uses eBPF — and it runs directly in the kernel.

Gecit just launched on Hacker News, and it demonstrates where internet freedom tooling is heading.

How it works:
→ Uses eBPF sock_ops to intercept packets at the kernel level
→ Fragments and reorders TCP packets to evade DPI signatures
→ No external proxy server needed — runs entirely on your machine
→ Zero overhead compared to VPN tunneling
→ Works against government-level censorship systems

Why this matters for data infrastructure:

DPI (Deep Packet Inspection) is the technology governments and ISPs use to identify and block specific types of traffic — including scraping, VPN connections, and proxy protocols.

The arms race between DPI systems and circumvention tools directly affects data collection:
1. Countries with aggressive DPI (Russia, China, Iran) block proxy traffic
2. ISPs use DPI to throttle or redirect automated requests
3. Corporate networks use DPI to detect unauthorized data access

eBPF-based bypass operates at a level that traditional DPI can't easily inspect. It's the equivalent of hiding in plain sight — the packets look normal, but they're not.

For anyone operating data infrastructure across borders: the tools for maintaining access are getting more sophisticated. And so are the systems trying to block them.

#Proxy #DPI #InternetFreedom
post_ru:

Gecit запущен на Hacker News и показывает, куда движутся инструменты интернет-свободы.

Как работает:
→ eBPF sock_ops перехватывает пакеты на уровне ядра
→ Фрагментирует и переупорядочивает TCP-пакеты для обхода DPI-сигнатур
→ Не нужен внешний прокси — работает полностью локально
→ Нулевой overhead по сравнению с VPN
→ Работает против государственных систем цензуры

Почему важно для data-инфраструктуры:

DPI — технология, которую правительства и ISP используют для блокировки трафика, включая скрейпинг, VPN и прокси-протоколы.

Гонка между DPI и обходом напрямую влияет на сбор данных:
1. Страны с агрессивным DPI блокируют прокси-трафик
2. ISP используют DPI для throttling автоматических запросов
3. Корпоративные сети детектят несанкционированный доступ

eBPF-обход работает на уровне, который традиционный DPI не может легко проинспектировать. Пакеты выглядят нормально — но это не так.

Инструменты доступа становятся сложнее. И системы блокировки тоже.

#Proxy #DPI #InternetFreedom

title: EU Data Protection Group Report on Legitimate Interest Under GDPR [pdf]
summary: Article URL: https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2026-03/spe-oss-case-digest-legitimate-interest_en.pdf Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47660063 Points: 3 # Comments: 0
editorial_override: EU GDPR Legitimate Interest report — regulatory framework for data processing
post_en:
The EU Data Protection Board just published its case digest on "Legitimate Interest" under GDPR. Every data company needs to read this.

Legitimate Interest is the legal basis most data operations rely on. This report tells you exactly how EU regulators are interpreting it in 2026.

Key takeaways:
→ Legitimate Interest can NOT be used as a blanket justification for data processing
→ The balancing test must be documented BEFORE processing begins
→ Data subjects' reasonable expectations are weighted heavily
→ Commercial interest alone is NOT sufficient — it must be "necessary"

What changed:
• Regulators are scrutinizing "legitimate interest" claims more aggressively
• The bar for "necessity" has been raised — you must prove no less intrusive alternative exists
• Cross-border data processing under legitimate interest faces additional requirements
• Automated decision-making based on legitimate interest has new restrictions

For data infrastructure companies:

If your data collection, proxy services, or scraping operations rely on "legitimate interest" as a legal basis — this report is your compliance roadmap.

The three questions every operation must answer:
1. Is the interest genuinely legitimate (not just commercially convenient)?
2. Is processing NECESSARY for that interest (no alternative method)?
3. Does it override the data subject's rights (documented balancing test)?

GDPR enforcement isn't theoretical anymore. It's specific, documented, and escalating.

#GDPR #DataProtection #Compliance
post_ru:

Законный интерес — правовое основание, на которое опирается большинство data-операций. Этот отчёт показывает, как регуляторы ЕС интерпретируют его в 2026.

Ключевое:
→ Законный интерес НЕ может быть общим оправданием обработки данных
→ Тест на баланс должен быть задокументирован ДО начала обработки
→ Разумные ожидания субъектов данных весят тяжело
→ Коммерческий интерес сам по себе НЕ достаточен — должна быть «необходимость»

Что изменилось:
• Регуляторы проверяют заявления о законном интересе агрессивнее
• Планка «необходимости» поднята — докажите, что нет менее инвазивной альтернативы
• Трансграничная обработка — дополнительные требования

Три вопроса для каждой операции:
1. Интерес действительно законный (не просто коммерчески удобный)?
2. Обработка НЕОБХОДИМА для этого интереса?
3. Она перевешивает права субъекта данных?

GDPR enforcement уже не теоретический. Он конкретный, задокументированный и эскалирующий.

#GDPR #DataProtection #Compliance

post_en:

Every year, these roundups shift. Here's what changed:

2022 lists prioritized: speed, price per request, proxy pool size
2024 lists prioritized: JavaScript rendering, anti-bot bypass, API simplicity
2026 lists prioritize: AI integration, structured data output, compliance features

The evolution is clear: scraping tools are becoming data delivery platforms.

What today's "best tools" have in common:
→ Built-in AI for data extraction (no more manual selectors)
→ Structured output formats (JSON, database-ready schemas)
→ Compliance documentation included with the product
→ Managed infrastructure (you don't run the proxies yourself)

What's disappearing from these lists:
→ Raw proxy providers with no scraping layer
→ Tools that require significant coding knowledge
→ Solutions without built-in bot detection handling

The market is sending a clear message:

Nobody wants to buy proxies and build a scraper. They want to describe the data they need and receive it clean, structured, and compliant.

The tools that understand this are growing. The ones that don't are becoming invisible in these comparison articles — which is where most buying decisions start.

title: Show HN: Mtproto.zig – High-performance Telegram proxy with DPI evasion
summary: Hey everyone. I built an MTProto proxy for Telegram aimed at bypassing active DPI censorship like the Russian TSPU. I chose Zig because it's perfect for writing fast network daemons and makes it incredibly easy to port low-level C bypass techniques like TCP desync and packet fragmentation. Would love to get some feedback or contributors! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47632692 Points: 23 # Comments: 14
editorial_override: High-performance Telegram proxy with DPI evasion — proxy infrastructure innovation
post_en:
A high-performance Telegram proxy written in Zig that evades Russian government-level DPI. Built by one developer.

Mtproto.zig implements the MTProto proxy protocol with TCP desync and packet fragmentation — techniques specifically designed to bypass the Russian TSPU (technical surveillance system).

The technical choices reveal infrastructure priorities:
→ Zig chosen for C-level performance without C's memory safety issues
→ TCP desync makes packet inspection return ambiguous results
→ Packet fragmentation splits protocol signatures across multiple frames
→ The entire system runs as a lightweight daemon — minimal resource usage

Why a Telegram proxy matters for data infrastructure:

Telegram is one of the largest platforms for real-time information flow — particularly in regions where traditional media is restricted. Russia, Iran, Belarus — millions of users rely on proxies to access it.

The same DPI bypass techniques apply broadly:
1. Any protocol can be fragmented to evade inspection
2. TCP-level manipulation is invisible to application-layer DPI
3. The cat-and-mouse between DPI and circumvention drives proxy innovation

Every technique built for censorship circumvention eventually becomes a tool in the broader proxy/infrastructure toolkit. Today's Telegram proxy techniques are tomorrow's general-purpose DPI evasion.

Innovation in internet freedom tools feeds directly into data infrastructure innovation. The connection is rarely discussed but always present.

#Proxy #Censorship #Infrastructure

title: When Virality Is the Message: The New Age of AI Propaganda
summary: Article URL: https://time.com/article/2026/04/02/when-virality-is-the-message-the-new-age-of-ai-propaganda/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47661231 Points: 11 # Comments: 7
editorial_override: AI propaganda and virality — AI-generated content trust crisis
post_en:
TIME Magazine: "When Virality Is the Message: The New Age of AI Propaganda."

The article documents how AI-generated propaganda has evolved from crude deepfakes to sophisticated, targeted content that's indistinguishable from authentic human posts.

The new propaganda playbook:
→ AI generates thousands of unique variations of the same message
→ Each variation is optimized for a specific platform and audience
→ Content is distributed through networks of AI-controlled accounts
→ Engagement metrics are manipulated to trigger algorithmic amplification

The scale problem:
• One operator can now produce more propaganda than entire Cold War-era state agencies
• Detection lags creation by weeks or months
• Platforms are overwhelmed — moderation can't keep pace

For the data industry, this creates a trust crisis at every level:

1. Social media data: How much is authentic? How much is AI-generated propaganda?
2. Web content: AI-generated articles are flooding news sites and blogs
3. Reviews and ratings: Synthetic manipulation is becoming undetectable
4. Training data: AI models trained on AI propaganda perpetuate the cycle

The value proposition of data infrastructure is shifting from "collect everything" to "verify everything."

Any data pipeline that doesn't include provenance verification is delivering contaminated output. And in 2026, the contamination is deliberate, sophisticated, and growing.

#AIPropaganda #DataQuality #ContentAuthenticity

title: Data DAOs for AI Training: Governance Models
summary: Data DAOs for AI Training: Governance Models    blockchain-council.org
editorial_override: Data DAOs for AI training governance — decentralized data ownership model
post_en:
Data DAOs for AI training. The concept sounds like Web3 hype — but the governance models are solving a real problem.

The premise: decentralized organizations that collectively own, license, and profit from training data used by AI companies.

Why this keeps gaining traction:

The current data economy is broken:
→ Individuals create data, platforms capture it, AI companies train on it
→ The value chain flows one direction — away from creators
→ No mechanism exists for collective negotiation
→ Individual opt-outs are meaningless at scale

Data DAOs propose:
1. Collective ownership: Members pool data assets into a shared governance structure
2. Licensing control: The DAO decides which AI companies can access the data, at what price
3. Revenue distribution: Training data licensing fees flow back to contributors
4. Transparency: On-chain records of who accessed what data, when, and why

The practical challenges are significant:
• Data verification and quality control at scale
• Legal recognition of DAO-based data licensing
• Competition with "free" scraped alternatives
• Technical infrastructure for provenance tracking

But the trajectory is clear: data ownership is collectivizing. Whether through DAOs, publisher cooperatives, or union-style organizations, individual data creators are organizing.

For data infrastructure: the shift from "collect and sell" to "license and verify" is accelerating. The next decade belongs to consent-based data infrastructure.

#DataDAO #AITraining #DataGovernance
post_ru:
Data DAO для обучения AI. Звучит как Web3-хайп — но модели governance решают реальную проблему.

Концепция: децентрализованные организации, коллективно владеющие, лицензирующие и получающие прибыль от training data для AI.

Текущая data-экономика сломана:
→ Люди создают данные, платформы захватывают, AI-компании обучаются
→ Цепочка ценности течёт в одну сторону — от создателей
→ Нет механизма коллективных переговоров
→ Индивидуальный opt-out бессмысленен в масштабе

Data DAO предлагают:
1. Коллективная собственность: участники объединяют data assets
2. Контроль лицензирования: DAO решает, кто получает доступ и по какой цене
3. Распределение дохода: лицензионные платежи возвращаются контрибьюторам
4. Прозрачность: on-chain записи доступа к данным

Практические вызовы значительны: верификация качества, правовое признание, конкуренция с «бесплатными» скрейпленными альтернативами.

Но траектория ясна: собственность на данные коллективизируется. Через DAO, кооперативы издателей или профсоюзные структуры.

Следующее десятилетие принадлежит consent-based data-инфраструктуре.

#DataDAO #AITraining #DataGovernance

title: AI agents pay USDC for API data via x402 micropayments – no API keys
summary: Article URL: https://x402.aigregator.com Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47651088 Points: 4 # Comments: 0
editorial_override: AI agents paying crypto for API data — machine-to-machine data economy
post_en:
AI agents are now paying for API data with cryptocurrency. No API keys. No accounts. Just micropayments.

x402 is a protocol that lets AI agents pay USDC for data access in real-time. One HTTP request, one payment, one response.

How it works:
→ AI agent sends a request with a payment attachment (USDC on-chain)
→ The data provider verifies payment and returns the data
→ No API key management, no account creation, no billing cycles
→ Each request is independently paid and authenticated

Why this is more than a crypto experiment:

AI agents have a fundamental problem: they need data from thousands of sources, but managing API keys and accounts for each one is a bottleneck.

x402 removes that bottleneck entirely:
1. An agent can access ANY participating data source instantly
2. Payment = authentication (no signup flows)
3. Costs are granular — pay per request, not per month
4. The agent manages its own budget autonomously

The implications for data infrastructure:

We're watching the first protocol designed specifically for machine-to-machine data commerce. Not humans buying API access. Machines paying machines for data.

This is what the "agentic web" actually looks like: AI agents with wallets, autonomously discovering data sources, paying for access, and integrating the results — all without human involvement.

The data economy is developing its own financial infrastructure. And it looks nothing like what came before.

#AIAgents #DataEconomy #CryptoPayments
